- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) after a peak, model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 2nd–4th week of forecast horizon; apply 2–4% upward bias for days 15–25.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, model lags; add 1–3% to forecast for days 10–20.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a peak (e.g., >10% fall), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days; add 1–3% to last 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
